t: The first great empire of the Deccan, ruling from Pratishthana (Paithan) and later from the Krishna valley.
Its ports and inland towns traded with the Roman world, and merchants funded Buddhist caves at Karle, Nashik and Kanheri.
Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Western Satraps c. 125 CE, but the empire fragmented in the early 3rd century.
dyk: Satavahana kings were known by their mothers' names, such as Gautamiputra, 'son of Gautami', and some of their silver coins bear legends in both Prakrit and an early Dravidian language.
ev: Simuka founds the dynasty in the northern Deccan (date disputed)
Queen Naganika's Naneghat inscription records Satakarni I's horse sacrifices
Gautamiputra Satakarni destroys the Kshaharata dynasty of Nahapana
Rudradaman I of the Western Satraps twice defeats the Satavahanas
Yajna Sri Satakarni recovers parts of the western Deccan
The kingdom fragments among the Abhiras, Ikshvakus and Chutus
